headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make CrewAI→n8n prompt/data leakage and cascading mis-execution plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and uses shared memory by default; n8n can read/write the server filesystem and execute workflow nodes. That creates a plausible file-based bridge where CrewAI output can be consumed as trusted content by n8n, enabling instruction injection. The pairwise pathway is documented only by profiles, so uncertainty stays medium rather than low.
conditions: IF CrewAI writes attacker-controlled text into a file that n8n later reads as workflow input
IF n8n workflow logic parses CrewAI output as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent's files
Add a provenance prefix to every handoff file
Require a human review step before n8n executes any CrewAI-produced text
Disable file-based handoffs and use a typed API payload instead
requires-engineering: add content-signing or schema validation at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while n8n processes whatever the workflow touches and stores credentials on its server. Both have filesystem access and broad network egress, so sensitive inputs can flow from CrewAI into n8n outputs or integrations in default setups. This is a realistic leakage path, though not enough evidence for high because no specific secret class is guaranteed.
conditions: IF the same sensitive document or secret is placed in both agents' working data
IF n8n workflow nodes transmit CrewAI-produced content to external services
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared working directories
Restrict n8n credentials to least-privilege scopes
Mask or redact sensitive fields before handoff
Turn off broad egress for the workflow where possible
requires-engineering: isolate each agent in separate containers with separate volumes

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write to their respective host-visible workspaces and broad subprocess/network capability. CrewAI uses per-process session scope with developer-defined shared state, while n8n shares state via datastore and connected systems. If they target the same mutable directory or integration, concurrent writes can corrupt files or overwrite workflow state; the default overlap is dangerous enough for high.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same directory or datastore
IF n8n workflow nodes and CrewAI tasks mutate the same external resource without locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes through a single queue
Disable concurrent runs for shared resources
Add file locks or optimistic concurrency checks
requires-engineering: move shared state behind a transactional store

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI can generate tool outputs and n8n can execute workflow nodes based on those outputs. Because n8n's AI Agent node orchestrates tools and Execute Command runs on the server, a bad CrewAI result can become an authoritative trigger for downstream actions without a built-in verification step. That makes cascading mis-execution plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF n8n consumes CrewAI output as a decision input
IF the workflow lacks an explicit validation or approval node before action-taking
mitigations: Insert a validation step before any action node
Require structured JSON with schema checks
Add a human approval gate for destructive actions
Log and diff CrewAI outputs before execution
requires-engineering: separate generation from execution into different workflows

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI is described as handling developer-passed crew data and API keys, while n8n processes whatever the workflow touches and stores per-credential secrets on its server. If regulated data is routed through both, retention and residency obligations can diverge across the pair. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated personal data or secrets are routed through both agents
IF the workflow's retention or logging settings differ between CrewAI and n8n
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through the pair
Align retention settings before deployment
Disable verbose logging for sensitive workflows
Document data residency for each integration
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement at the workflow boundary
